title: The workforce is sized by capability gaps, not by a headcount target
context: ADR-0004 set the roster at one hundred agents and, in the same decision, moved anti-sprawl out of headcount and into mechanical checks: duplicate and near-duplicate measurable outputs fail the build, as do duplicate success metrics, unresolvable reporting lines, agents that can only read, and expensive models outside four named roles. Those checks are the real control and they work. The fixed count was a second, redundant guard that contradicted the first: RosterIsExactlyOneHundredAgents asserted the roster was exactly 100 while the tests beside it were already proving that every role was distinct, reachable, funded and able to act. The founder has since revoked the numerical target outright. Its practical effect was to make the studio unable to staff a capability it had discovered it was missing -- GAP-0001 records one, found by inspection rather than by argument: nothing in the roster owns the studio's own operating tools, and no dormant record could ever be activated to cover it. A roster that cannot grow to meet a demonstrated need is not disciplined, it is stuck.
decision: The roster has no fixed size. It may grow above one hundred or shrink below it, and neither direction is a goal. The controls that replace the count are the ones ADR-0004 already named, plus two this decision adds. First, a new role requires a filed capability gap under Studio/state/gaps carrying evidence, the agents considered and rejected as owners, and the reason activating a dormant agent or widening an existing scope does not answer it -- activation is always the cheaper answer and must be ruled out explicitly. Second, retirement becomes accountable in the same way hiring is: a retired agent must state retiredBecause and retiredAt, mirroring existsBecause, and retirement is a status change rather than a deletion because other agents' dependsOn and challenges lists still name the id. All 100 existing records are preserved, the 70 dormant ones included; they hold no budget and are not emitted as definitions, and dormancy remains the normal state for a role whose precondition has not fired. Nothing here changes who may act: Studio/constitution/** remains human-exclusive under permissions.json, so creating, retiring or replacing an agent is still a founder edit, and filing a gap record grants no authority to perform one.
consequences: The studio can now staff a demonstrated gap and can retire a role without deleting its history. The cost is that the distinctness checks carry the whole anti-sprawl load alone, so they are strengthened rather than left as they were: the duplicate-output, near-duplicate-output and cheap-model-majority checks now ignore retired agents, because a retired role was otherwise able to block its own successor from ever claiming its measurable output, which would have made the roster grow-only in practice while appearing to support retirement. A proposed specialist inside a gap record is checked against the live roster for duplicate outputs before it becomes an agent, which moves the duplicate catch from after creation to before it. This supersedes the roster-size clause of ADR-0004 only; that decision's division structure, its distinctness checks and its cost discipline are untouched and remain in force.
